records.name: 1807 & Friends, Inc.
records.notes: Not a group you can join. The public role is buying concert tickets: a Monday evening series at AVA, 1920 Spruce Street. The school outreach program (presentations by ensemble members, with the King David's Harp program) is for schools, and the funding named on the page targets parochial schools. Newest past concert listed: 2026-10-05. Verdict not_a_group under the ticket-only rule.

records.name: Arch Street Meeting House Preservation Trust
records.summary: The trust that cares for the Arch Street Meeting House, a historic Quaker meeting house in Center City. It runs the museum, guided tours, and a list of public talks and events.
records.what_you_do: Visit the museum, book a student or group tour, or come to one of the listed talks and events. The site does not describe a volunteer program or membership.

schedule.text: Museum open Thursday to Sunday, 10 am to 4 pm. Listed events run October to December 2026 on the upcoming events page. The Sunday 10:30 am meeting for worship is run by a separate Quaker group that meets in the building.

cost.text: Admission is on the museum hours page, which was not read in full

first_step.how: Visit the museum Thursday to Sunday, 10 am to 4 pm, or book a student or group tour from the tours page.
first_step.basis: The museum is open to walk-in visitors on a published schedule, and tours have their own page.

records.notes: The batch address (1515 Cherry Street) differs from the building address the site gives (320 Arch Street). The site address is used. The Monthly Meeting of Friends of Philadelphia (archstreetfriends.org) meets in the building; it is a worship group and was not checked in this lane. The Friends Pantry (historicasmh.org/friendspantry) is named on the site and was not checked. Volunteer and membership roles are not described.

records.name: Asian Americans United
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit, founded in 1985, that builds leadership in Asian American communities. It runs youth leadership programs, the Mid-Autumn Festival, culture and storytelling projects, and civic and immigrant rights work.
records.what_you_do: Take part in a youth leadership program, help with the Mid-Autumn Festival or another event, sign up to volunteer through the site's volunteer form, or join its civic and immigrant rights work.

schedule.text: The Mid-Autumn Festival is an annual event. The 2026 festival is announced on its own page, but the date was not shown in the text read. Youth program schedules are not listed on the pages read.

cost.text: Not stated on the pages read

first_step.how: Sign up on the volunteer form linked from the Get Involved page, or email aau@aaunited.org to ask about the Youth Leadership Development Programs.
first_step.basis: The volunteer sign-up and the email contact are public, but program deadlines are not listed.

records.notes: Status is active because the site announces the 2026 Mid-Autumn Festival. The month was not shown, so last_sign_of_life is left out. The events page lists no dated events. Program pages linked from the site were not read in full.

records.name: Asian Arts Initiative
records.summary: An arts center on Vine Street with exhibitions, performances, artist residencies, and youth arts workshops. Kids and teens can take arts workshops and leadership programs, and anyone can attend the shows and events.
records.what_you_do: Kids and teens can take the Youth Arts Workshop or the Youth Leadership Initiative, or come to a summer camp (Camp Bruce Lee is listed). Adults can attend exhibitions, performances, and community events. Membership and volunteer roles are not described on the pages read.

schedule.text: Gallery open Thursday to Saturday, 2 to 6 pm. Events and workshops have their own dates on the programs page, such as the Artist Town Hall on October 19, 2026.

cost.text: Some events are free (pay what you wish). Ticketed events are listed at about $15 to $25.

first_step.how: Come to the Artist Town Hall on October 19, 2026 (6 to 8:30 pm, free, pay what you wish), or ask about youth workshops through the contact form at /about/contact-us.
first_step.basis: Public events have set dates and prices. Youth workshop sign-up is described only as a link.

records.notes: The current exhibitions open September 4, 2026 and run to December 5, 2026. The Careoke Club event is on October 9, 2026 with tickets through Eventbrite. The youth program pages linked from the site were not read.

records.name: Association for Public Art
records.summary: A Philadelphia organization that runs public art programs, including Art on the Parkway, and keeps a public art map and an archive of public art from 1872 to 1980.
records.what_you_do: See the public art on view, such as Let Freedom Ring at Cherry Street Pier and Franklin Thread in Maja Park, come to a listed event or tour, or use the public art map. Class and volunteer roles are not described.

schedule.text: Events and tours are posted on the Events and Tours page, which was not read. Public works on view run through October 2026, and Let Freedom Ring through November 1, 2026.

first_step.how: See Let Freedom Ring at Cherry Street Pier before November 1, 2026, or join the mailing list on the site to hear about tours and events.
first_step.basis: The outdoor works can be seen at any time and the mailing list is public, but the event sign-up route was not shown.

records.notes: Mainly a public art organization, so the public way in is attending. No classes, membership, or volunteer roles were found. The Events and Tours page was not read, so event dates beyond the two installations are unknown.

records.name: Azuka Theatre Collective
records.summary: A Philadelphia theater company that stages productions and develops new plays with writers. Its New Play Development program offers readings, events, and a way to submit scripts.
records.what_you_do: See a production (tickets are set by the viewer after the show), come to a New Play event, or submit a script through the New Play Development pages. Classes, usher volunteering, and open rehearsals are not described; ask the company.

schedule.text: Productions run through the 2026 to 2027 season, and each show has its own dates. A production titled #CHARLOTTESVILLE runs October 14 to November 1, though the year is not shown on the page.

cost.text: Pay What You Decide: the viewer sets the price after the show

first_step.how: Buy a Pay What You Decide ticket for the next production through the tickets link on the site, or join the mailing list to hear about New Play events and script submission periods.
first_step.basis: Anyone can buy a ticket with a flexible price. The writer programs accept submissions, though the open periods were not shown.

records.notes: The dated items on the homepage are mostly press previews and reviews of the company's shows (2026-09-01 to 2026-09-28), plus older reviews from 2025 and 2026. The company's own season pages were read on the homepage only.

records.name: Bearded Ladies Cabaret
records.notes: The public roles are buying tickets (a timed entry to the current exhibit, and Saturday 8 pm cabarets), donating, and buying merchandise. The associate artists page describes an advisory board of current members, with no application or open role. No classes, membership, or volunteer roles were found. Verdict not_a_group under the ticket-only rule. The footer shows only a copyright year, which is not used as evidence. Recheck if a community program opens.

records.name: Black Pearl Chamber Orchestra
records.summary: A Philadelphia chamber orchestra that gives concerts and runs community programs. The Inreach programs include a conducting program, an open rehearsal, and a leadership program that bring people closer to the musicians and the creative process.
records.what_you_do: Attend a concert from the performances list, go to an open rehearsal, or take part in an Inreach program (iConduct! or Orchestrating Leadership). The sign-up details for these are on their own pages.

schedule.text: Concerts are listed on the performances page. The next dated listing is Handel's Messiah with the Jeremy Winston Chorale on December 20, 2026, at Salem Baptist Church of Abington.

cost.text: Prices are on each performance listing, which was not read

first_step.how: Go to the performances page and book the December 20, 2026 Messiah concert at Salem Baptist Church of Abington, or ask about the open rehearsal through the contact page.
first_step.basis: Concerts are public and the site describes open rehearsals, but the sign-up route for the rehearsal was not shown.

records.notes: The newest dated item is an upcoming concert (2026-12-20), so last_sign_of_life is the month of that listing. The site gives no street address. The batch address (30 S 15th Street) is not confirmed on the site, so no location is published. The orchestra has no matching tag in the vocabulary, so interests are left empty.

records.name: Blue World Gallery
records.notes: The site says the gallery is under construction. It gives no classes, hours, address, contact details, or events, so there is no public way in yet. Hidden for now as having no public way in. Recheck later. Supporters named on the page (House Museum, Scribe Video Center, the Mellon Foundation, the Philadelphia Cultural Fund) were not checked.

records.name: Britt Fishel & Artists Inc
records.notes: A dance company. The public roles are buying tickets to performances (the Kulturfactory event in Italy in August 2026, and a Philadelphia premiere listed for September 2026 with no set date) and donating. The & Space program offers subsidized space to emerging choreographers and screendance artists, so it is for artists who apply, not for the public. The site lists no classes, workshops, open rehearsals, membership, or volunteer roles. Verdict not_a_group under the ticket-only rule. Recheck if a public program opens.

records.name: BYO Printmaking Collaborative
records.summary: A printmaking studio in Old City with equipment for screen printing, etching, relief printing, and book arts. Members share the studio, and the public can visit it on First Fridays.
records.what_you_do: Visit the studio on First Fridays (5 to 8 pm), book a visit at other times, follow the open calls for prints, or apply to become a member who uses the studio.

schedule.text: First Fridays, 5 to 8 pm, open to the public. Other visits by appointment.

cost.text: Membership fees are not shown on the pages read

first_step.how: Come to the next First Friday open studio, 5 to 8 pm, at 12 N 3rd St, #5, or email byostudio.philly@gmail.com to ask about a visit or membership.
first_step.basis: The site describes First Fridays as open to the public. Membership needs an application, so that route is not open to everyone.

records.notes: The open calls and the events calendar carry no dates on the homepage. The events page the site links to returned 404 when tried, so the calendar was not read. Classes and volunteer roles are not described.

records.name: Cardell Dance Projects
records.notes: The website could not be read. The TLS certificate does not match the host (both www and the bare domain fail). This is not a bot check and was not bypassed. Nothing about classes, performances, or joining was verified. The batch also lists the aka Scrap Performance Group. The batch address (726 N Uber St) was not confirmed on a source page, so no location is published. Recheck the site later.

records.name: Center for Emerging Visual Artists
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit, founded in 1983, that supports emerging visual artists through a fellowship, citywide exhibitions, and community outreach. It also runs the Philadelphia Open Studio Tours, where visitors see artists' studios.
records.what_you_do: Tour artists' studios on the Philadelphia Open Studio Tours, or volunteer for the tours. You can also see the exhibitions, go to events such as the ART PARTY and auction, or join as an artist member. The site lists outreach to older adults and a Hand-in-Hand community program.

schedule.text: The Philadelphia Open Studio Tours have a 2026 directory and map (tour dates not read). Events are on the Upcoming Events page.

locations.label: Mailing address (mail only, per the site)
locations.address: The Philadelphia Building, 1315 Walnut Street, Suite 300

cost.text: Tour and event costs are not stated on the pages read

first_step.how: Join the mailing list on the site, then look at the POST 2026 directory and map to find studios on a tour. The site's POST page lists volunteer roles.
first_step.basis: Several public ways in are listed (mailing list, tours, volunteer page), but the pages read give no event dates.

records.notes: The newest evidence is the 2026 POST directory and map, dated by year only. The upcoming events path guessed on the site returned 404, so the event list was not read. The batch address for this group looks like a residential apartment, so it was not used. The mailing address from the site is used instead.

records.name: Chestnut Street Singers
records.summary: A cooperative chamber choir in Center City that sings a wide range of music, from Renaissance works to new pieces. Singers are unpaid volunteers who sing in two concerts a season and help run the group.
records.what_you_do: Sing in the choir after an audition, or attend a concert. This season's audition dates have passed, so the next chance to sing is a spring audition window, which the site does not date.

schedule.text: Rehearsals on Mondays, 7 to 9 pm, at Children's Community School, 1212 S 47th St. The fall cycle runs from late August to November 9, and the spring cycle from late January to May 3. Concerts: November 14, 2026 at 7 pm, and May 8, 2027 at 4 pm.

cost.text: No fees for singers, who are unpaid volunteers. Limited help with costs is available case by case.

first_step.how: Attend the fall concert on November 14, 2026 at 7 pm. To sing, email auditions@chestnutstreetsingers.org and ask when the spring audition window opens.
first_step.basis: Singers apply and audition (about 20 minutes, with scales and sight-reading), and the choir is recruiting by voice part this season. Concerts are open to all.

records.notes: The newest evidence is upcoming concerts (2026-11-14 and 2027-05-08), so last_sign_of_life is the month of the nearest listing. The site gives no concert venue address, and the batch address (2125 Chestnut St) is not confirmed on the site, so it is not published. The rehearsal zip is not given and is left out.

records.name: Chinese American Women’s Sisterhood Society of Philadelphia
records.notes: The grantee list gives no website or social link, and web search was not allowed in this run, so nothing about the group was checked. The grant is listed for 2026 under Art and Culture (multi-disciplinary). The batch address has a unit number, and it was not published because it is not confirmed as a public address. A web search for the group is needed in a later run.

records.name: Cosmic Writers
records.summary: A nonprofit that uses writing to help children become creative and critical thinkers. It offers free one-on-one coaching for young writers, a drop-in writing night, and classroom help for teachers.
records.what_you_do: Young writers can get free one-on-one coaching (matched to a coach who knows their genre, with sign-ups reopening in January 2027), or drop in on Friday Night Writes (Fridays 4 to 6 pm, online or in person at Gutmann College House). Families can also buy a writing activity book for $9.95 and try it at home.

schedule.text: Friday Night Writes is a drop-in on Fridays, 4 to 6 pm, starting September 25 in the fall (year not stated on the page). Cosmic Coaching meets weekly for eight weeks, with times set between the coach and the writer.

cost.text: Cosmic Coaching is free. The cost of Friday Night Writes is not listed.

first_step.how: Reserve a virtual slot for Friday Night Writes through the Google Form linked on the Cosmic Writers site. Cosmic Coaching sign-ups are closed for fall 2026 and return in January 2027.
first_step.basis: Friday Night Writes is open to young writers with a simple slot reservation. Coaching is closed until the new term.

records.notes: The newest dated item on the homepage is the 2025 Annual Report, dated by year only, so the status is probably_active. The batch address is a mailbox-style number that the site does not list, so it is not published. The site says its newsletter sign-up may not work yet.

records.name: Da Vinci Art Alliance
records.summary: An artist collective founded in 1931 by Italian immigrants. It runs a gallery, exhibitions, workshops, a monthly book club, and mentoring for artists. Visitors can see shows, come to openings, and join as members.
records.what_you_do: Visit the gallery, come to an opening or the monthly book club, take a workshop such as the Paper and Paste wheat paste class, or join as an artist or supporting member. Volunteers can join a committee.

schedule.text: Gallery open Fridays and Saturdays, 11 am to 6 pm. Wednesday, Thursday, and Sunday visits by appointment. The site footer lists Thursday and Sunday hours, so check before going. The monthly book club meets 4 to 5:30 pm, for example October 21 and November 18, 2026.

cost.text: Prices for workshops and openings are not stated on the pages read. Memberships are offered.

first_step.how: Come to the book club on October 21, 2026 (4 to 5:30 pm) or the opening reception on November 7, 2026 (5 to 7 pm). For membership, see the Join our Collective page.
first_step.basis: Gallery visits and events are public, with a published calendar and membership options. The steps to join the book club or a workshop were not shown.

records.notes: The calendar lists many dated events from 2026-10-08 to 2026-12-20. The Paper and Paste workshop is on October 10, 2026, 1 to 4 pm, and its sign-up method was not shown. The Icebox Project Space events use a second space whose address is not listed separately.

records.name: Dolce Suono Ensemble
records.summary: A chamber music group founded in 2005 that performs a concert series at Trinity at 22nd, tours, premieres new works, and makes recordings. It also lists education and community projects.
records.what_you_do: Buy a ticket to a Sunday afternoon concert at Trinity at 22nd, or donate. The site lists young composer and student projects (ComposerLab Flute, an online lecture series, a young composers competition, and a community project in Spanish), but does not explain how to join them.

schedule.text: Concerts at 3 pm at Trinity at 22nd, 2212 Spruce Street: October 11, 2026; December 6, 2026; February 14, 2027; and June 13, 2027. All four are Sundays.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket for the Sunday, October 11, 2026 concert at 3 pm (titled Poulenc Woodwind Masterworks), or ask the ensemble about its education projects through the contact page at dolcesuono.com/contact/.
first_step.basis: Concerts are sold to the public with set dates and prices. The education projects are listed without steps to join.

records.notes: Published rather than not_a_group because the site lists education and community projects, though the joining steps were not found. Chamber music has no matching tag in the vocabulary, so interests are left empty. The email address is hidden on the site, so only the phone and contact page are listed.

notes: 18 batch groups: publish 14, not_a_group 3, hide 1. Searches used: 0 (budget 0). Fetches used: 31 of 60. Failures: two first attempts hit a shared rate limit and passed on a single retry (Bearded Ladies, BYO); Cardell failed on a TLS mismatch both times; several guessed event URLs returned 404 or a redirect and were followed once. The grant list facts come from the harvested lead file (harvested 2026-10-04) and each lead's source_url. Deliberately not published: batch addresses that look like apartments or mailboxes (Center for Emerging Visual Artists, Cosmic Writers, Chinese American Women's Sisterhood Society) and grantee-list addresses not confirmed on the group's site (Black Pearl, Cardell, Chestnut). Arch Street: the batch address (1515 Cherry Street) differs from the site's building address (320 Arch Street); the site address is used. Named but not checked (outside this arts lane, so not added as leads): Monthly Meeting of Friends of Philadelphia (archstreetfriends.org, meets in the Arch Street building), Scribe Video Center (a supporter named by Blue World Gallery), Jeremy Winston Chorale (performs with Black Pearl), Folk Arts-Cultural Treasures Charter School (named by Asian Americans United).
